text:
noah: Heads up - planning a return from parental leave on 9/1 and Im requesting a compressed schedule: 4 days/week at 0.8 FTE for 10 weeks. Will this affect my health plan premiums or HSA contributions? Also curious about vacation accrual during the phased period.

sara-people-ops: Hi Noah — good question. Health premiums: if you stay on company benefits and are on payroll, premiums continue as usual. If youre unpaid and off-payroll for any segment, premiums may move to direct-bill or be paused; well flag it. HSA: employer contributions correlate with pay periods. If youre paid at 0.8 FTE and on payroll, employer HSA contribution will prorate.

oliver-payroll: Vacation accrual: accrual is based on pay status and FTE. For 0.8 FTE, accrual rate is 80% of full-time accrual while on payroll. If unpaid, accrual pauses. Please send LOA payment status so we can compute exact accrual.

rebecca: Also note some benefits (transit, commuter) require minimum participation; check the benefits portal for details on enrollment changes.

emma-manager: For coverage, I suggest a rotating on-call reduction for the first 4 weeks. @noah can you list your top 3 recurring responsibilities and Ill assign temporary owners?

noah: Top tasks: 1) infra deploy review 2) weekly partner sync 3) incident triage. I can keep partner sync and hand off the first two for 4 weeks.

leave-bot: Reminder: phased returns require manager sign-off and People Ops approval. Please submit the phased return form at least 10 business days before your scheduled return.

sam-people-ops: Adding that vacation carryover rules still apply; if you are below the carryover cap we can be flexible for that review period.

noah: Thanks all — uploading the phased return form now and will confirm pay status with payroll.
